Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Common Implementations

Several patterns implement backpressure:

- **Bounded queues**: A queue with fixed capacity blocks the producer once full, preventing further writes until the consumer drains items. This is a synchronous, implicit signal.
  
- **Credit-based flow control**: The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. Credits are consumed as data flows and replenished as the consumer processes items, giving fine-grained control over emission rates.
  
- **Reactive-pull models**: Instead of the producer pushing items to the consumer, the consumer requests items on its own schedule. This inverts the control flow and ensures the producer only emits when explicitly asked.
